findings.title: Missing re-check after acquiring write lock, and the diff may leave unlocked writes or stale reads

response:
## 1) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: Missing re-check after acquiring write lock, and the diff may leave unlocked writes or stale reads

Affected:
- pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:41-49

Explanation:
The write lock is taken after the read lock is released, and the cache is not re-checked once it is held. Concurrent callers that all see a nil cache will each take the lock in turn and recompute the assets, repeating file I/O and JSON parsing. Correctness is preserved, but the double-checked pattern is incomplete.

In Dev mode, `Lock()` is taken on every call. This serializes all requests that fetch web assets for the whole function body, which includes file reads. That is a performance regression compared with before, though it is limited to dev environments.

The rest of the function is outside the diff, so I cannot confirm that the later assignment to `entryPointAssetsCache` happens while the lock is held. It should be, because the lock is held by `defer`. Any early return paths must also not bypass it.

Also, `ret` is a shared pointer returned to callers. If any caller mutates the returned struct, a data race remains. That is a risk only if callers mutate it.

Proposed fix:
~~~go
entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock()
defer entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Unlock()
if cfg.Env != setting.Dev && entryPointAssetsCache != nil {
    return entryPointAssetsCache, nil
}
~~~

true_positives.golden_comment: The GetWebAssets function implements an incomplete double-checked locking pattern for caching web assets. The function first checks if the cache is populated using a read lock (RLock), and if the cache is empty, it acquires a write lock to populate it. However, it fails to re-check whether the cache was populated by another goroutine while waiting to acquire the write lock.
true_positives.matched_candidate: Missing re-check after acquiring write lock - concurrent callers that see nil cache will each recompute assets, repeating file I/O and JSON parsing
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate issue identifies the exact same problem as the golden comment - the missing re-check after acquiring the write lock in a double-checked locking pattern. Both comments point out that without re-checking the cache after acquiring the write lock, multiple goroutines that saw an empty cache will each recompute/populate the assets, leading to redundant work (file I/O and JSON parsing). This is the same underlying concurrency bug.

false_positives.candidate: In Dev mode, Lock() is taken on every call which serializes all requests that fetch web assets including file reads, causing performance regression
Cannot confirm that assignment to entryPointAssetsCache happens while lock is held - early return paths must not bypass the lock
Returned pointer 'ret' is shared between callers - if any caller mutates the returned struct, a data race remains

false_negatives.golden_comment: In addition to the missing double-check, the function has a critical flaw in its error handling: it unconditionally assigns the fetch result to the cache (line 69: entryPointAssetsCache = result) regardless of whether the fetch succeeded or failed. When an error occurs during asset fetching, result is nil, and this nil value overwrites any previously valid cache entry.
